---
title: "The Reviewer's Code"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Send Small, Say So. **Objective:** review work that involved an LLM, kindly and effectively, and choose formats that review well.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">General practice, not a vendor claim. Team norms you agree locally override these defaults.</span>
:::

You will also be on the receiving end. Reviewing LLM-assisted work is the same craft as any review, with a few shifts in attention.

- **Ask for the evidence.** "Which test shows this works?" works better than "are you sure?".
- **Watch for the usual tells.** Plausible but unused code, tests weakened to pass, and confident comments that do not match the code.
- **Ask for understanding.** "Can you explain why this branch exists?" is fair for any author.
- **Say when it is too big.** "Please split this" is a legitimate review comment, and the Wall of Output taught why.
- **Be kind.** The aim is better science, so keep the tone friendly and aim at the work, not at catching a person out.

## Formats that review well

Notebooks are one example. A [marimo](https://marimo.io/) notebook is stored as a plain `.py` file, so a diff shows what changed. A Jupyter `.ipynb` is JSON that also stores outputs and run counts, so diffs are noisy and hard to read, though stripping tools exist. If you ask an agent to produce analysis, prefer a format your reviewer can actually diff.

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Jupytext](https://github.com/jupytext/jupytext): jupytext project (GitHub), repo. Why read: it pairs an .ipynb with a plain .py, which is the format to ask a collaborator for when you will review their notebook.
- [nbdime](https://nbdime.readthedocs.io/en/latest/): nbdime project, docs. Why read: it gives notebook-aware diff and merge tools if you must keep .ipynb in Git.
:::
